related_questions.question: What to take if you're COVID positive?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, focus on at-home care with rest, fluids, and over-the-counter medications for symptoms like fever and cough. For those at higher risk of severe illness, prescription medications like oral antivirals may be an option and should be discussed with a doctor immediately. Treatment should be started within 5-7 days of symptom onset for best results.
snippet_highlighted_words: rest, fluids, and over-the-counter medications for symptoms like fever and cough

list.title: Rest and Hydration:
list.snippet: Get plenty of rest and drink lots of fluids to help your body fight the infection.

list.title: Symptom Relief:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help manage fever and pain. Cough syrups or lozenges can also provide relief.

list.title: High-Risk Individuals:
list.snippet: People at higher risk of severe illness (older adults, those with certain medical conditions, etc.) may be eligible for prescription medications like oral antivirals. These medications can help prevent mild illness from worsening.

list.title: Consult a Doctor:
list.snippet: It's crucial to consult with a doctor to determine the best course of treatment, especially if you are at higher risk or if your symptoms are severe. They can assess your individual needs and prescribe appropriate medication.

list.title: Early Treatment is Key:
list.snippet: If you are eligible for antiviral medications, starting treatment within 5-7 days of symptom onset is crucial for effectiveness according to the CDC.

list.title: Isolate and Prevent Spread:
list.snippet: Stay home and isolate yourself from others to prevent further spread of the virus.
